# realloc_growth.cr: grow an IO::Memory to t bytes by 1 KiB writes, ns per build.
# sp = threads spinning beside it (same process, same 4 CPUs, taskset -c 4-7).
# Columns: off = GCRY_REALLOC_MOVE=0; N = move when the old block's data pages
# hold at least N bytes (a temporary override of Heap::REALLOC_MOVE_MIN).
# Staged move (DONTUNMAP to a kernel-chosen address, then grow-move into the new
# chunk), 3 runs per row.

# Earlier pass, move from 64 KiB on (the first cut of the threshold), by size:
# sp=0: 96 KiB 41.9k → 38.4k ns; 128 KiB 47.5k → 44.4k; 256 KiB 86.9k → 72.8k;
#       512 KiB 162k → 120k; 1 MiB 298k → 201k; 4 MiB 1.29M → 676k.
# sp=3: 96 KiB 119k → 138k; 128 KiB 132k → 149k; 256 KiB 204k → 231k;
#       512 KiB 318k → 343k; 1 MiB 497k → 496k; 4 MiB 1.79M → 1.21M.
# Every mremap flushes the TLB of each CPU the process runs on; with three
# busy threads that IPI cost outweighs the copy below ~256 KiB of old data.
